posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Twig_the_Blue_Pikmin said:
It seems to say it's YEP's Core Engine rather than the Battle Engine I believe with the thing on the far right?
Click to expand...
YEP_CoreEngine is unrelated: it modifies the error-reporting method to show the trace in-game, that's why it's showing there.
The error seems to be back to what it was in
post #5
, which is promising. This error makes me think that the
BattleManager.startAction
method is setting the current
_subject
to
null
, because this is the core method (rpg_managers.js) giving rise to the error (comments by me):
JavaScript:
BattleManager.processForcedAction = function() {
    if (this._actionForcedBattler) {                // if true, forced battler is not null
        this._turnForced = true;
        this._subject = this._actionForcedBattler;  // so cannot be null here
        this._actionForcedBattler = null;
        this.startAction();                         // so must be set null here
        this._subject.removeCurrentAction();        // to cause that error here
    }
};
You're manipulating the action via the
<Custom Action Start Effect>
tag of Buffs & States Core, which hooks into
startAction
. However, I don't see you doing anything obvious to change the battle manager subject in that notetag, and the code itself seems to be straight from
Yanfly's Paralyze Tips & Tricks article
...
That said,
the STB plugin is unsupported
. You could try testing:
With only 3 plugins turned on (for the Paralyze notetag):
YEP_BattleEngineCore, my fix, and YEP_BuffsStatesCore.
With only 4 plugins turned on (STB system enabled):
YEP_BattleEngineCore, my fix, YEP_X_BattleSysSTB, and YEP_BuffsStatesCore.
(Note that you can press Ctrl+A in the Plugin Manager to select all plugins, then right-click -> Turn OFF to turn them all off at once.
I suggest testing in a copy of your project
, rather than the real thing. Alternatively you could try to reproduce the relevant setup in a new project, without all the extra plugins & content complicating things.)
If it errors out even in case 1, then I'm not sure what's happening.
If it works in case 1 but not in case 2, I'd guess it's an issue with forced actions in STB?
If it works in case 1 and case 2, check your other plugins. I'd start with battle-related stuff.
As always, remember to save your project to apply Plugin Manager changes before testing, and make sure you Yanfly's plugins are loaded in the recommended order, listed on Yanfly's site:
Category:Yanfly Engine Plugins - Yanfly.moe Wiki
www.yanfly.moe
It's also possible you are using outdated or edited core scripts. More info below in case you want to check that~
Spoiler:
info on how to check/update core scripts
Choose Game -> Open Folder from the editor's menu bar;
Open the
js
subfolder there;
Open e.g.
rpg_core.js
in any text editor (Notepad is sufficient).
You'll see something like this at the top, unless it's really old:
//=============================================================================
// rpg_core.js v1.6.2
//=============================================================================
Functionally, I don't think the core scripts have changed since v1.6.1? If you're using an older version, or if you have edited any core script files at any point, you can update your project by carefully following the instructions in this announcement:
Announcement - RPG Maker MV - v1.6.1 Stable Release!
6/21/2018 Everyone, please read the instructions carefully. The bugs that are being reported shouldn't happen if the correct files were even copied properly. Such examples like the "CTRL BUG" shouldn't happen if you copied index.html, package.json, the rpg*.js files and so on.  I also received...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Maybe someone else has more ideas. Either way, good luck!

posts.body:
Twig_the_Blue_Pikmin said:
I have some bosses in my game that will perform an Action after hitting a certain percentage of their HP while I also have States in the game that can cause the Actor or Enemy inflicted to Act but have it cancelled before anything is done if the chance for it to happen is rolled. The chance calculation uses this notetag in the State:
And it seems whenever it activates during a Force Action command in the Battle Events, it makes this error show up
View attachment 363408
So is there anyway I could fix this while still keeping the State acting the same way, I wouldnt mind if the Forced Action were to ignore the Paralyze Chance but I dont want it to just remove the State from the Enemy so it doesnt break the game, I'd just want it to like ignore the whole process for any Forced Actions if possible
Click to expand...
I FINALLY SOLVED THIS! KINDA! BUT IT WORKS NOW!
Basically it seems whenever a Force Action is triggered in a STB Battle after EVERYONE has performed an Action, the Error is caused. Force Action seems to work perfectly fine when triggered DURING the Turn as the Turn doesnt count as over till everyone finishes their Actions, and the Turn being over is what causes the Error soooo, I made the Troop Event rely on the Condition of having a Switch turned On to be able to run and then plugged in these codes(?) into the notetag of a Paralyze State!
<Custom Turn End Effect>
$gameSwitches.setValue(ID, false);
</Custom Turn End Effect>
<Custom Respond Effect>
$gameSwitches.setValue(ID, true);
</Custom Respond Effect>
Click to expand...
Now when the Turn Ends if the Enemy has the Paralyze State, it'll turn that Switch OFF before any damage is done thus preventing the Error from occuring, then with the Custom Respond Action the Switch will be turned back ON the second an Actor damages the Enemy so that the Troop Event with the Force Action will trigger DURING the Turn rather than the Turn End as to allow everything to work!
Thank you everyone for helping me as much as yall did, i dont think I would've figured out this work around if it werent for yall! :>
